content.thinking: I need to fix the citations to reference F1, T9, and T14 only, and avoid spelling out specific numbers like "503" or "24" directly—using phrasing like "an error status" or citation references instead to keep the raw digits out of the root cause explanation.

action_items.item: Make a product decision on the account page during a payment provider outage. For example, render it with a card-unavailable notice and checkout disabled, with the docstring and the test that pins the current behaviour changed on purpose.

Add a detection signal on the payment provider dependency, such as the rate of error responses from card lookups or a provider status check, so a provider outage is identified as such before the shop's error-rate alert fires.

Write an upstream-outage runbook for io-shop covering contacting IO Payments Ltd, shopper-facing messaging, and verifying recovery once the provider answers successfully again. Consider adding a safe mitigation for Argus where the product allows one.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers requesting the account page mostly got a failed page. The error rate rose from {errors_before} to {errors_while_broken} on average and peaked at {errors_at_worst}, from {began}. The alert fired at {alert_raised}, {alert_raised - began} after onset, which includes the {rule_waits} the paging rule waits.

The failing requests were logged as PaymentProviderFailed: the payment provider api.io-pay.example returned {Gbf7d.1} for the card lookup at payment_provider.py:95. The same error was logged throughout the broken period.

The page fails when the lookup fails because it needs the card and only io-pay holds it. The code turns the provider's answer into a failed page instead of showing the page without the card. The Code-Fix reading says this is deliberate, because checkout would fail too while the provider is down. This comes from a static reading of the code and was not verified by running anything.

io-pay itself began returning errors at the onset. The record does not show why. It rules out a change on our side: no production changes in the {T8.2} hours before the onset, no flag changes at the flag provider, and the Code-Fix reading found nothing in io-shop that touches the payment path. The evidence stops at the provider.

contributing_factors.factor: The account page has no degraded mode when the payment provider is down. A provider outage turns directly into failed pages, and whether to show the page with a card-unavailable notice has not been decided.
No alert on the health of the payment provider dependency was seen in the record. The page came only from the shop's own error rate, after the paging rule's wait.
Argus has no mitigation that answers an upstream dependency failure. It refused to act and the incident was escalated while the service was still failing, and no runbook for this case was seen.

input.executive_summary: From {began}, shoppers who opened their account page mostly got an error instead of the page. The error rate averaged {errors_while_broken} while the service was broken and peaked at {errors_at_worst}, against {errors_before} beforehand. The service was still not back to normal when the incident was closed, so it was broken for at least {duration}. The cause was an outage at the external payment provider, which holds the shopper's card details that the page needs. Nothing had changed in our own service. Argus identified the provider as the cause, found no safe mitigation or code fix it could apply, and escalated to a human.

went_well: The log line named the provider host, path and status, so the investigation pointed at the upstream dependency within seconds.
Argus did not make a change that could not help: it refused to act, found no code fix, and escalated to a human.
went_wrong: The incident was closed as escalated with the service not back to normal, and nothing Argus could do reduced the impact.
Detection depended only on the shop's own error rate, so there was no earlier signal from the provider.

input.root_cause: The third-party payment provider io-pay answered card lookups with a {Gbf7d.1} error status, and the io-shop account page cannot render without the card. By a documented product choice it fails the whole page instead of degrading. The record does not show why io-pay failed. The code reading that describes the deliberate failure was static and not run.
input.symptom: Account pages failed for most shoppers
